correctness.rationale: Exact pairwise Euclidean squared distances yield thresholds 1,2,3. Four exhaustive maximal-clique families yield a cone cover, precisely 8 binomial(n,3) exceptional long triangles, a short-root crosspolytope sphere, and one mixed bridge for every signed edge. Descending free-face collapse of cones gives a subdivided crosspolytope graph; the exceptional triangles attach its 2-skeleton. Both maps from the connecting graph into simply connected U and S are null, so the homotopy pushout is U wedge S^(n−1) wedge suspension(G); in degree two the 8 binomial(n,3) spheres follow exactly and integrally. The actual embedded verifier was run for n=3,4,5,6 and checked geometric facets and mod-two chain ranks. Its finite scope is not substituted for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The exact statement has new geometric objects and additional mixed attachments beyond the closest prior claims. Verified comparisons cover the type-D long-root-only homotopy claim, type-A roots, cuboctahedral finite cases, and full primary texts of circle and hypercube Rips papers. The short-root coning plus bridging triangles yield a different integral homotopy wedge and are not implied by any inspected stronger theorem. Search incompleteness is acknowledged rather than portrayed as uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The complete unequal-length root configuration of Coxeter type B has a canonical Euclidean filtration. The theorem gives a uniform nontrivial first homotopy transition from a cycle wedge into a mixed sphere wedge, with an exact cubic rank and an intrinsic high sphere explained by the signed crosspolytope. This structural gluing is not a trivial restatement of long-root-only Betti numbers and is useful as a natural root-family persistence benchmark. It is meaningful without claiming later-scale persistence or stronger equivariance.
